exposure: Timing of decision to receive neuraxial labor analgesia (a priori vs. as a last resort vs. not at all)
outcome: Breastfeeding initiation success, defined as exclusive breastfeeding until discharge associated with postnatal weight loss <7% at 60 hours from birth
cohort: Women who delivered singleton cephalic newborns vaginally and were willing to breastfeed at a single Italian baby-friendly hospital (n=3,628, of whom 775 received neuraxial analgesia)
finding: Compared to women who tried to cope with labor pain, an a priori choice of neuraxial analgesia was negatively associated with breastfeeding initiation success.
